subject: business-studies

moments.title: The Motivation to Work
moments.body: Herzberg's interviews with Pittsburgh engineers and accountants distinguish hygiene factors (which prevent dissatisfaction) from motivators (which cause satisfaction).
moments.takeaway: Job satisfaction and dissatisfaction may have different causes.

moments.title: One More Time: How Do You Motivate Employees?
moments.body: Herzberg's Harvard Business Review article becomes one of HBR's most reprinted, popularising 'KITA' management.
moments.takeaway: HBR articles can outlast academic books in shaping practice.

moments.title: Job characteristics model
moments.body: Hackman and Oldham develop a more empirically robust model of intrinsic motivation through skill variety, task identity, autonomy and feedback.
moments.takeaway: Successor models replaced Herzberg in research.

now.title: Motivation in modern work
now.body: Job design, autonomy, and intrinsic motivation continue to draw on the Herzberg lineage. Remote and gig work challenge the framework.
now.open_questions: How do gig workers' hygiene and motivator factors differ from traditional employees?

reflection: Herzberg's two-factor model is widely taught and contested in equal measure.
